archetype:court-knight.line: Crowley's Knight is the Yod of the Name and the Father of the pagan series. The tie to the Wise Old Man is a reading made here.

sections.title: The letter of the Name
sections.line: Crowley gives the four courts the four letters of the Name, and the Knights the first of them.

quotes.text: The Knights represent the powers of the letter Yodh in the Name.
These cards constitute a pictorial analysis of the powers of the four letters of the Name and the four Elements.

sections.title: Father, Mother, Son, Daughter
sections.line: Crowley sets the courts as the series Father, Mother, Son and Daughter, and contrasts it with the Hebrew scheme.

quotes.text: It has been thought better, for the present pack, to adopt the term “Knight”, “Queen”, “Prince” and “Princess”, to represent the series Father, Mother, Son, Daughter, because the doctrine involved, which is extraordinarily complex and difficult, demands it.
The Hebrew system is straightforward and irreversible; it postulates Father and Mother from whose union issue Son and Daughter.

sections.title: The Knight as Father
sections.line: Crowley says the Father is Knight because he rides, and that the Hermit's Yod is the Father who is Wisdom. The tie to the Wise Old Man rests on that Wisdom, and is a reading made here, not an equation Crowley states.

quotes.text: The Father is “Knight” because he is represented as riding on a horse.
The letter Yod is the first letter of the name Tetragrammaton, and this symbolizes the Father, who is Wisdom;
The moral qualities appropriate to this figure are activity, generosity, fierceness, impetuosity, pride

quotes.text: The Princesses represent the Hé final of the Name.

sections.title: Daughter in the series
sections.line: Crowley names the Princess the Daughter of the pagan series, and places the Daughter on the throne of the Mother in the Ace of Disks.

quotes.text: The Princess is not only the perfect Maiden, but, owing to the death of the Prince, the forsaken and lamenting Widow.

the letter Tau upon the Tree of Life appears as an emanation from the moon of Yesod, the foundation of the Tree and representative of the reproductive process and of the equilibrium between change and stability, or rather their identification. archetype:seven.line: Seven is the company of planetary gods, read through alchemy's metals and the Gnostic archons, with Pauli's dream-reading beside it.

sections.title: What Jung names
sections.line: The seven stands for the planetary gods, and in the language of initiation for the highest stage. Jung gives no essay on seven; the number is named where he discusses planets, metals and initiation.

Originally the seven stars were the seven great Babylonian gods, but at the time of Enoch’s revelation they had become the seven Archons
Its connection with the seven metals implies a connection with the seven planets, so that the tree becomes the world-tree

archetype:ten.line: Ten is the completed cycle and the unfolding of unity; the tetraktys and von Franz's whole multiplicity stand beside it.

family:air.line: Jung names air as a light outer element, as pneuma in the spiritual sense, and as the link between fire and water.

sections.title: What Jung names
sections.line: The defining words first: an alchemical author's description of air, then air among the four, then air as the volatile element above earth.

quotes.text: What our author has to say about the element of air is significant in this respect: The air is a pure uncorrupted element, in its kind the most worthy, being uncommonly light and invisible, but inside heavy, visible, and solid.

Second vertical series: The earth emerges from the chaotic waters of the beginning, from the massa confusa, in accordance with the ancient alchemical view; above it lies air, the volatile element rising from the earth.

quotes.text: Since pneuma, like spirit, originally meant air in motion, this designation sounds archaic or else deliberately physicistic.

It is clear that wind is air, and air is life, and life is soul, that is, oil and water.

quotes.text: From the darkness of the unconscious comes the light of illumination, the albedo.

quotes.text: From this the washing (ablutio, baptisma) either leads direct to the whitening (albedo), or else the soul (anima) released at the “death” is reunited with the dead body and brings about its resurrection, or again the “many colours” (omnes colores), or “peacock’s tail” (cauda pavonis), lead to the one white colour that contains all colours.
Salt as much as ash is a synonym for the albedo (or dealbatio), and is identical with “the white stone, the white sun, the full moon, the fruitful white earth, cleansed and calcined.”

quotes.text: Therefore the artist must wait until he sees the Tincture covered over with its other colour, as with the whitest white

family:citrinitas.line: The yellowing as Jung names it: one stage of the older four-colour scheme, which he says was later dropped and never described on its own.

sections.title: What Jung names
sections.line: The yellowing as the xanthosis, otherwise called the citrinitas, one of four stages in the older scheme.

quotes.text: Four stages are distinguished (fig. 114), characterized by the original colours mentioned in Heraclitus: melanosis (blackening), leukosis (whitening), xanthosis (yellowing), and iosis (reddening).
Later, about the fifteenth or sixteenth century, the colours were reduced to three, and the xanthosis, otherwise called the citrinitas, gradually fell into disuse or was but seldom mentioned.

sections.title: Why the scheme was reduced
sections.line: Jung gives a general reason for the reduction to three colours, not one that singles out yellow.

quotes.text: Since the process never led to the desired goal and since the individual parts of it were never carried out in any standardized manner, the change in the classification of its stages cannot be due to extraneous reasons but has more to do with the symbolical significance of the quaternity and the trinity; in other words, it is due to inner psychological reasons.

Whereas the original tetrameria corresponded exactly to the quaternity of elements, it was now frequently stressed that although there were four elements (earth, water, fire, and air) and four qualities (hot, cold, dry, and moist), there were only three colours: black, white, and red.

sections.title: The transition to the reddening
sections.line: Jung's placings of the yellowing: the transition to the reddening, the direct route from whitening to reddening, and a dream commentary where yellow coincides with the reddening.

quotes.text: The transition to the rubedo is formed by the citrinitas, though this, as we have said, was omitted later.
The rubedo then follows direct from the albedo as the result of raising the heat of the fire to its highest intensity.
In alchemy yellow (citrinitas) often coincides with the rubedo.

These three appear in three colours which precede the redness: the body, or earth, in Saturnine blackness; the spirit in lunar whiteness, like water; and the soul, or air, in solar yellow.

family:earth-element.line: Jung puts earth as the fourth element in one passage and as a fifth in another, and as the black basis of the work.

sections.title: Fourth or fifth
sections.line: Jung states both positions without resolving them; in the Axiom of Maria fire and earth stand at the two ends, with no interaction between them.

quotes.text: Earth occupies the central position as the fifth element, though it is not the quintessence and goal of the work but rather its basis, corresponding to terra as the arcane substance in Western alchemy.
The synthesis of the incorruptible One or quintessence follows the Axiom of Maria, the earth representing the “fourth.”
Fire comes at the beginning and is acted on by nothing, and earth at the end acts on nothing.
Between fire and earth there is no interaction; hence the four elements do not constitute a circle, i.e., a totality.

sections.title: Basis and seed-bed
sections.line: Earth is the arcane substance, the prima materia that a spirit inhabits, and the black field in which gold or lapis is sown.

quotes.text: The alchemical earth, as we saw, is the arcane substance, here equated with the body of Christ and with adamah, the red earth of paradise.
According to Basilius Valentinus, the earth (as prima materia) is not a dead body, but is inhabited by a spirit that is its life and soul.
It is then the black earth in which the gold or the lapis is sown like the grain of wheat

sections.title: Nigredo as terra nigra
sections.line: Jung reads the blackness of the first stage as earth, terra nigra.
